question: Clinicians score gooseflesh as one item on a standard bedside scale. Which condition does that scale measure?
answer: Opioid withdrawal. The Clinical Opiate Withdrawal Scale grades gooseflesh alongside sweating, yawning, a running nose and wide pupils, because the sympathetic nervous system rebounds as opioids wear off and raises the skin's hairs. It is one proposed origin of the phrase cold turkey. A nurse can grade withdrawal partly by looking at a forearm.
move: Ask what else can pull the same lever as the obvious cause.
trap: Picking hypothermia, because cold is what gooseflesh always suggests.
source: Wesson and Ling, J Psychoactive Drugs, 2003
reference: Wesson and Ling, The Clinical Opiate Withdrawal Scale (COWS), Journal of Psychoactive Drugs, 2003
